final_vote_record.note: Press reports the same tally for Basic Law Amendment 14, the Deficit Reduction Law (Amendment 24) and the 2023 supplementary budget without saying whether they were voted on together; outside the vote tables' coverage.

deviations: The Knesset website (main.knesset.gov.il, knesset.gov.il OData, and fs.knesset.gov.il directly) returned a geo-restriction maintenance page; the gazette PDFs were read from Internet Archive captures (via curl and macOS PDFKit, because the WebFetch tool cannot reach web.archive.org), and government composition was taken from Wikipedia articles on the 31st, 33rd, 34th, 35th, 36th and 37th governments, as the sheet allows when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Dates of first and final readings were taken from the Knesset's plenum records as mirrored by Open Knesset (kns_plmsessionitem.csv, kns_plenumsession.csv at production.oknesset.org/pipelines/data/plenum/), and bill identifiers and summaries from the mirrored legislation database (kns_bill.csv, kns_documentbill.csv). These are Knesset data through a mirror the sheet names for laws; I treated them as Knesset records.

Vote tables: the Open Knesset mirror (view_vote_rslts_hdr_approved_extra) was consulted directly for seq 89, 97 and 101 to see the sequence of recorded votes; it confirms the sheet's extracts and ends on 13 July 2021.

Explanatory notes were reachable only for seq 112 and seq 118 (archived first-reading bill PDFs); for the other ten the bill PDFs and the Knesset record (Divrei HaKnesset .doc files) were not archived and the Knesset server is blocked, so named_beneficiary was coded from the enacted text and, where present, the Knesset database's law summary.

Not found: the recorded tally for seq 76 (no electronic vote in the tables; no press report located); named vote breakdowns for seq 112 and seq 118 (coalition_only left blank); whether one vote approved both laws in seq 89 and the final-approval tally for seq 97 (press 62-38 vs. second-reading 63-37).

No page about a court case was opened. Search-result listings included links to a court opinion (Versa) and advocacy/IDI pages; none was opened. The Hebrew Wikisource header of Basic Law: The Government cites a HCJ case number; the Wikisource pages were used only for gazette citations and links.
No files were written anywhere; all work was done in memory per the invoking instruction, so the sheet's scratch-subfolder step was not performed.
